 Colorado weather: Up to 10 inches of snow forecast for mountains 
 More than a foot of snow possible Wednesday on the high-end of the forecast, according to NWS

 By Lauren Penington | lpenington@denverpost.com | The Denver Post PUBLISHED: November 4, 2026 at 7:14 AM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Another round of snow is headed for Colorado’s mountains on Wednesday, dropping up to 10 inches on some of the state’s highest peaks, according to the National Weather Service.
 As of Wednesday morning, expected snow totals included, according to the weather service :
 1 inch in Conifer, with up to 2 inches possible
 2 inches in Georgetown and Woodland Park, with up to 4 inches possible
 2 inches in Aspen, with up to 6 inches possible
 4 inches at the Keystone Ski Area Summit, with up to 5 inches possible
 4 inches at the Eisenhower-Johnson Memorial Tunnel, with up to 6 inches possible
 4 inches on U.S. 6’s Loveland Pass and U.S. 50’s Monarch Pass near Gunnison, with up to 8 inches possible
 5 inches in Breckenridge, with up to 8 inches possible
 5 inches on Interstate 70’s Vail Pass, with up to 14 inches possible
 6 inches in Fairplay, with up to 15 inches possible
 6 inches in Leadville, with up to 18 inches possible
 8 inches on Colorado 91’s Fremont Pass near Leadville and Colorado 9’s Hoosier Pass near Breckenridge, with up to 20 inches possible

 Winter weather advisories will be in effect for Boulder, Chaffee, Clear Creek, Eagle, Gilpin, Grand, Lake, Park, Pitkin and Summit counties between 2 p.m. Wednesday and 5 a.m. Thursday, according to the weather service.
 The storms will intensify Wednesday afternoon south of I-70 and continue overnight, forecasters said . Rain is forecast for Colorado’s valleys.
 Forecasters expect 3 to 10 inches of snow in the mountains of Summit County and the Mosquito Range, 4 to 9 inches in the Sawatch Mountains and 4 to 8 inches in the Gore and Elk Mountains, the advisories stated.
 This is a developing story and may be updated.
